purpose: Explain the precise legal effect of an approved property event separately from the factual event, with applicable law, conditions, registration requirements, exceptions, temporal version and explicit non-effects.
core_principle: FACTUAL EVENT → APPLICABLE LAW → CONDITIONS → REGISTRATION/EFFECT REQUIREMENTS → LEGAL EFFECT → NON-EFFECTS
rules: A factual event is not itself the legal effect.
The exact applicable legal provision or authoritative case-law proposition must support the stated effect.
Amendment date is not automatically commencement date.
Historical effects use the law applicable at the relevant time, including transitional provisions where material.
Conditions, exceptions, provisos and savings remain visible.
Registration requirements are distinguished from contractual execution or physical possession.
A legal effect is not stated beyond the scope supported by evidence and authority.
The system explicitly identifies material things the event did not establish or accomplish.
A document may evidence an event without proving the final registered legal state.
Conflicting evidence or unresolved legal authority prevents a definitive effect.
hard_stops: Never infer legal effect from event name alone.
Never use current law for historical effect without verification.
Never treat inheritance entitlement as registered ownership.
Never treat sale as automatic security discharge.
Never omit a material exception or condition.
Never state a definitive effect when required evidence is missing.
Never create a new legal conclusion merely through display rendering.
